verdict: ntilt.py is a correct implementation of the pre-registered T/F design, and the stored T/F numbers can be trusted as such: tau=0 reproduces std.engine and mfeng mode 1 exactly, an independent plain-Python version matches T1 and F1 on the real path to 1e-14 relative, and all 1,629 values in pre_T_le2014.json and pre_F_le2014.json re-compute with zero difference. I found no look-ahead and no accounting error in what tau>0 adds. The one material problem is in the input, not the engine: the single seed-11 draw of the synthetic pre-1999 night residual has a realised mean of -7.9%/yr on dev250_path and -3.0%/yr on the real path instead of 0, so "mode C" is harsher than stated; this costs T1 about 2.6%p on dev250_path and 0.85%p on the real path. With that residual de-meaned, still 0 of 9 T/F candidates beat v1 on both bases under C or M, so the verdict stands, but the dev250_path magnitudes for always-on tilts are too pessimistic and the M-mode failures are close calls. T1 loses under C because fees (-3.6 to -3.8%p), financing (-3.0%p) and the idle 15% futures account (-1.0%p dev, -3.6%p real) together outweigh the post-1999 premium (+6.2 to +6.9%p); no design-fairness sensitivity turns T1 positive on both bases under C or M.

findings.title: Engine is correct against its specification
findings.detail: Read line by line against beng.run1 and mfeng.run1F: the tau=0 code paths are identical, and what tau>0 adds does what the pre-registration says. Tilt is sized at close t from equity at close t, the level in force that night and 20-day vol through t-2; it earns ron[t+1]; fee is charged at entry on Y and at exit on Y*(1+ron); financing is 0.8132*(rf+0.4%/252); futures tax is 11% of yearly net P&L above D with no carry-forward, paid from the futures account; no tilt is opened on the last day; final value includes both accounts and both liquidation taxes.
findings.evidence: a10_causal.py: a change to ron[j], r[j] or rf[j] first moves equity on day j, never earlier; a change to sg[j] first shows at j+3 (sizing at j+2). T4 reacts to night returns only when v1 is flat, T5 only when v1 holds. Pulse test: +1% night gives exactly tau*E[j-1]*1% for F1 and exactly the cap (0.15/0.12 = 1.25) for T1. Cost test: tilt P&L equals minus fees, and minus financing, to 8 decimals.

findings.title: Seed-11 residual draw makes mode C harsher than 'alpha = 0' on dev250_path
findings.detail: Each source day before 1999-03-10 gets one fixed synthetic residual (ms1f.split_source, seed 11). Its realised mean is -7.9%/yr on the dev250_path source rows and -3.0%/yr on the real path, and the bootstrap reuses the same rows so it does not average out. Other seeds give -2.3 to +0.2%/yr on dev. This inflates the losses of always-on tilts on dev250_path: T1 by 2.6%p, F1 by 4.7%p, F2 by 8.3%p in mode C. The pass/fail verdict does not change (0 of 9 under C and under M after de-meaning), but in M five T candidates turn positive on dev250_path and fail only on the real path.

findings.title: Why T1 loses under C
findings.detail: On the real path the idle 15% futures account alone costs 3.62%p (v1 runs on 85% of equity, re-set yearly), and the tilt itself nets -0.19%p: premium +6.85 and beta exposure +1.14 are eaten by fees -3.76, financing -2.99, futures tax -0.73 and residual -0.71. On dev250_path idle cash costs 1.03%p and the tilt nets -2.63%p, of which 2.6%p is the seed-11 residual mean. Night variance on top of 3x TQQQ costs 2.2 to 2.9%p and is embedded in those steps.

findings.title: T4 carries the idle futures account all year although its tilt is on 12-14% of days
findings.detail: Idle cash alone (phi 0.15, tau 0) is -1.08%p dev / -3.62%p real of T4's -1.58 / -5.22. A version funded only while v1 is in cash was not run (run budget); subtracting the idle part leaves about -0.5 / -1.6%p. F3, the no-idle futures analogue, shows the same: -0.56 / -1.41%p relative to v1-as-futures. So the handicap is real but does not change the result.
findings.evidence: a8_sens.py reference rows; stored T4 and F3 values

findings.title: Design choices tested as unfair to the tilt do not rescue it
findings.detail: Halving phi to the broker minimum with no buffer improves T1 by 2.0%p (dev C) and 3.4%p (real C) but stays negative and is not operable. The yearly sweep is favourable, not unfair: monthly is 2.0%p (dev) and 1.8%p (real) worse in C. Relaxing the margin cap is worse. Sweep gain realisation costs 0.2 to 0.4%p, futures cash at 0% costs 0.2%p. With everything tilt-unfriendly removed at once T1 is still -1.45 / -0.13 in C.

findings.title: Design choices tested as favourable to the tilt are small, except the fee level
findings.detail: A 1% of notional penalty on the nights where the futures account is under 7% of notional at the open costs 0.02 to 0.09%p. Whole MNQ contracts at 80M KRW shrink the tilt (average 0.35 dev / 0.65 real) and make d less negative. Extra slippage is the stored fee-x2 run: another 0.83bp per side costs T1 2.9%p (dev) and 3.0%p (real). No intra-night liquidation is modelled and cannot be with daily data.

findings.title: Fee assumption is the largest single lever
findings.detail: 0.83bp per side is 4.18%/yr of notional and costs T1 3.5 to 4.1%p. Whether a real MNQ round trip is cheaper than that today was not checked against any broker schedule. Interpolating between my fee=0 run and the base run, half the fee would put T1 near -1.9 / -2.0 in C and about +0.2 / -0.3 in M.
findings.evidence: interpolation is INFERRED from a6_decomp.py fee=0 runs

findings.title: F family: v1's brake reacts to the tilt
findings.detail: In impl 1 the brake is fed the whole futures account, so tilt losses cut v1's level (2.03 to 1.57 on dev C). That accounts for 2.6%p of F1's dev C loss and 0.4%p on the real path. In T the brake sees only the stock sleeve's unit value and flows are not read as performance.

findings.title: v1 inside T is not bit-identical to stand-alone v1 on bootstrap paths
findings.detail: On the real path the trade count is identical (155). On dev250_path only 15% of paths have the same trade count and the mean absolute difference in average level is 0.019, with no systematic sign (median 2.052 vs 2.050). Cause: the tax deduction D is a fixed amount applied to a smaller sleeve, plus sweep tax and cost, which shift the unit value slightly.

findings.title: Cosmetic items
findings.detail: The night share is rounded to 0.8132 (effect 1e-6 on CAGR). The recorded daily equity excludes that evening's entry fee, which shows one day later (no effect on the final value). The sweep takes cash before TQQQ instead of pro rata (+0.03 to +0.17%p). The label tau=1.0 overstates the realised tilt (0.79 to 0.85) because the margin cap binds about half the time.
findings.evidence: indep.py with exact constant; a10_causal.py; a6_decomp.py

open_issues: The seed-11 residual artefact sits in ms1f.split_source, so the ms1f lane should confirm it and check how much it moves P1-P3; I measured it only through the T/F engine.

Beyond the six item-4 sensitivity runs I ran two input-noise checks: four other seeds on T1 (mode C) and one de-meaned-residual variant for all nine candidates (C and M). They are checks on the stored numbers, not candidates.
A T4 variant that funds the futures account only while v1 is in cash was not run (item-4 budget used); the 'still fails' statement for it is inferred from additive differences and from F3.
Real MNQ all-in cost per side was not verified; the M-mode verdict is sensitive to it, the C-mode verdict much less.
Intra-night margin calls cannot be tested with daily data; I could only count nights where the account is under 7% of notional at the open print.
The independent re-implementation covers continuous sizing only; whole-contract rounding (notional>0) was checked by reading and by one run, not re-implemented.
Dividends are ignored on both sides by convention; the +0.2 to +0.3%p estimate for T1 is not a run.
My scripts set NUMBA_CACHE_DIR to /home/user/onv/wf2/audit_ntilt/nbcache so nothing was written outside the lane folder.
